title: 1:1 prep - Diego Ramirez (AE) - 2026-03-04
body:
Purpose: quick sync with Diego to review top accounts, escalations, capacity constraints, and next actions. Keep it tight (30 min).

Context/notes before the call:
- Diego running 8 active enterprise accounts (booked ARR ~ $3.2M). Quarter close in 3 weeks - two expansion deals at risk (Acme Corp, BrightWave).
- Recent incidents: Acme reported a spike in inference latency on Redwood Dedicated (ticket CS-4217). Engineering triage says possible batching misconfig on their side + model variant mismatch.
- BrightWave: CSAT dropped after rollout of quantized model (lossy outputs for few production prompts). They asked for rollback.
- Diego flagged bandwidth: onboarding new dedicated cluster for FinTech customer next week; wants short checklist for Private deploy handoff.

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick personal check-in (2-3 min) - energy, blockers for week
2) Top account review (10 min)
   - Acme Corp: current status, ask from AE/CSM, deadline to resolve latency before UAT next Tue
   - BrightWave: rollback status + mitigation plan (QA prompts to validate)
3) Ops items (8 min)
   - Dedicated cluster handoff checklist readiness for FinTech (who owns infra runbook?)
   - Escalation path clarity for next time (SRE, Eng-on-call, support SLAs)
4) Career/checkpoint (3 min) - runway for Diego's promotion MBOs (customer expansions, docs)
5) Action items + confirm owners (2 min)

Prep notes & talking points:
- Acme: remind Diego to share the exact request trace IDs from the latency window (time range: 2026-03-01 09:00-11:00 PST). Ask if they changed batch_size or enabled continuous batching toggle recently. If not available, ask Diego to request server logs and client config.
- Ask Diego to run a quick A/B test: same prompt to quantized vs fp16 variant, capture 10 sample responses and scoring rubric; I'll help draft the rubric.
- For BrightWave rollback: propose staged rollback: 1) pin model to previous (v1.9) for 20% traffic, monitor quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/heuristic scoring + two lead prompts), 2) if green after 24h, increase to 100%. Need Diego to own comms with customer and schedule a short review with Eng + Applied ML.
- Dedicated handoff checklist (high level items to confirm with infra team):
   * customer has VPC peering set up + allowed CIDR ranges
   * KMS/HSM keys exchanged and tested (encrypt/decrypt test)
   * baseline perf test run (p95 latency, throughput target) and baseline report uploaded to Confluence
   * deployment runbook + rollback steps are in shared repo; Diego to confirm links
   * support rotation and escalation contact list shared with customer

Draft action items (explicit, owner, due):
- Diego: get Acme trace IDs and client config, push to CS-4217 ticket (due 2026-03-05)
- Avery: draft A/B scoring rubric for BrightWave quantized vs fp16 (due 2026-03-05)
- Diego + Applied ML (Maya Patel): schedule 30m quick QA session for BrightWave sample prompts (target 2026-03-06)
- Diego: confirm Dedicated handoff runbook links and post to Confluence page listed in linked_artifacts (due 2026-03-08)
- Avery: open a short RFC for the staged rollback procedure template we can reuse across accounts (draft by 2026-03-10)

Risks / questions to surface:
- If Acme is modifying client batching config mid-UAT, that could mask platform issues - need to lock client-side settings during investigation.
- BrightWave QA: do we have a reliable automated metric for hallucination/regression? If not, need a lightweight human-in-loop check for the staged rollback window.

Notes to self (post-call):
- Follow up on CS-4217 with eng triage owner (add to ticket: request kernel logs + model variant metadata)
- Remind SRE to add p95 latency dashboards for Acme dedicated pool (new tile on per-customer dashboard)

Quick reminders / template lines to use on the call:
- "Wanted to align on a minimal rollback plan that limits customer risk and gives us quick signal (24h) before a full rollback."
- "If you can drop the trace ids and configs into the ticket during the call, I'll ping eng to prioritize triage."

End of doc.
